text:
incident-bot: :pager: PAGED: p99 tail latency spike detected on continuous-batching path in us-west-2 — p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.8s, streaming stalls observed across a subset of workers. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

Sam: saw the alert, jumping in. Are we seeing increased batch sizes or packer stalls?

Priya: noticing mixed seqlen variance up ~4x from baseline in the last 10m. A few packs are hitting max_batch_size and then backing up.

Mateo: customer-facing check: webhooks for a single high-throughput tenant show long reply times. No obvious 5xxs. Might be degradation not full outage.

Lin: quick tell — streaming stall logs show repeated "kv-cache-miss -> blocking-evict" on the cont-batch runner. That lines up with long-tail due to cache churn.

Sam: good catch. Initial mitigation options: reduce max_batch_size on contpacker, force packer to prefer smaller packs, enable pack-shed for streaming lanes, or route heavy tenant to dedicated pool. Thoughts?

Priya: do the first 2 immediately: 1) set max_batch_size to 32 (was 128) for streaming-affine queues, 2) enable pack-shed for streamers. That should lower p99 fast.

SREPager: Sam you're on-call. Please coordinate mitigation and update customer-impact status.

Sam: on it. Applying packer config change now. Running:```sh
# reduce batch size for streaming-affine packs
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://ops-api.internal/configs/contpacker -d '{"streaming_max_batch":32}'
```

ops-bot: config update accepted by config-service; rolling change to 6 worker pods.

Mateo: pinging customers: one large tenant (tenant_id=acme-42) has increased tail latency, they're the bulk of traffic on these queues. Escalating to Solutions for heads-up.

Lin: also toggling kv eviction policy to be slightly more aggressive to cut churn — running safe evict experiment on subset of workers.

Priya: parallel step — enable pack-shed:```json
{"packer": {"streaming": {"pack_shed": true, "min_pack": 4}}}
```ops-bot will apply.

ops-bot: pack-shed toggle applied to streaming pools; changes hit in ~30s.

Sam: monitoring metrics — p95 dropped from 420ms -> 180ms within 90s, p99 trending down from 2.8s -> 900ms. Streaming stalls count decreased. :thumbsup:

Mateo: customer ACME reports improvement for some requests but still seeing occasional long tails. They're still concerned. We should consider short-term routing of their traffic to a dedicated capacity if we can.

Priya: agree. If they have heavy bursts with long sequences, contbatch will amplify. Routing them to dedicated small-GPU pool (or a smaller-sequence-optimized model) is safer. Can we spin up a reserved micro-pool?

ops-bot: provision request queued. ETA ~ 8 minutes for a tiny dedicated node in us-west-2.

Lin: note for postmortem — sequence length distribution shows a heavy tail from ACME's new feature that concatenates user histories; we should add a per-tenant seqlen cap or recommend prefix truncation in docs.

SREPager: please make customer-impact doc entry and set severity. Status: partial degradation, single tenant affected, mitigation in progress.

Sam: updating status page and the incident ticket. Adding links and note: temporary config changes (streaming_max_batch=32, pack_shed=true), kv-evict tuning, dedicated micro-pool pending.

Mateo: ACME moved ~60% traffic to the dedicated micro-pool — their p99 now ~210ms. They're happy for now but asked for a postmortem and a mitigation plan.

Priya: next actions before close: 1) revert streaming_max_batch to baseline slowly after we deploy a better pack-selection heuristic; 2) add per-tenant seqlen monitoring + alert; 3) prepare tenant routing runbook (how to move heavy tenants to reserved capacity).

Lin: I'll capture the logs and dump the problematic pack traces: `grep "pack-id" /var/log/contpacker/* | grep acme-42` and attach to the ticket.

Sam: agreeing on runbook items. I'll create a short action list in the incident ticket and assign owners.

ops-bot: config audit: streaming_max_batch changed by Sam -> new value 32, pack_shed toggled true by Priya, kv-evict policy bumped on subset by Lin.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, p99 dropped 2.8s -> 210ms for affected tenant. Customer notified. Postmortem required.

Mateo: marked for postmortem, assigning Priya (root cause analysis) and Lin (remediation/automations). Sam will own runbook + customer comms.

Sam: closing monitoring loop — will let this thread know when we revert or if any regressions. Thanks everyone.

Priya: final note — consider a medium-term change: adaptive batch-size knob that considers per-tenant seqlen variance rather than global max. Saves us from manual toggles. Filing RFC. :eyes:

SREPager: ack, incident downgraded to resolved state in pager after customer acceptance.

Sam: thread closing — moving to postmortem workspace. Link added to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3172

ops-bot: automated reminder set to follow up in 72h for postmortem draft.

Lin: thanks all, good rapid mitigation.
